answer: Sybil resistance can rest on scarce physical receipts. Each epoch an agent must visit a kiosk in a shopping oasis, where a clerk scans a one-time code and the terminal signs it. Terminals have a monthly quota and are paid per visit, so an attacker cannot mint them; owner standing is at risk. A thousand wallets need a thousand signed visits across many kiosks. Each receipt is a nullifier, single-use, like light through a prism. Weight is marble-hard, credited only where the terminal passes audit. Attack cost is rent, staff time and quota from parties it cannot control, renewed per epoch.
